title: Cover the Board With L-Shaped Pieces

concept.title: Cover the first empty square, with each of the four turns of the L
body: An *L-tromino* covers three squares of a 2 by 2 block (the block without one corner), so it has 4 orientations. As with dominoes, count the tilings by always covering the **first empty square in reading order**: whatever piece covers it, this square must be the **first square of the piece in reading order**. So each orientation can be described by the offsets of its three squares from its first square.

body.code:
SHAPES = [
    [(0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 0)],     # the 2x2 block without its bottom right corner
    [(0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1)],     # without its bottom left corner
    [(0, 0), (1, 0), (1, 1)],     # without its top right corner
    [(0, 0), (1, -1), (1, 0)],    # without its top left corner: the first square is the top right one
]

body: For every orientation check that the three squares are inside the board and free, cover them, recurse, and uncover them. Holes (`#`) are covered from the start. Compared with the domino problem, the only change is the list of pieces: the **same search** works for any set of shapes, which makes this method the standard way to attack tiling puzzles.

statement: A board has `r` rows and `c` columns; some squares are holes (`#`), the others are free (`.`). A piece is an L-tromino: it covers three squares of a 2 by 2 block, in any of its 4 orientations. Count the ways to cover every free square with pieces that do not overlap and do not cover holes. Two tilings are different if some piece is different.
inputFormat: Each of the next `r` lines has `c` characters, `.` or `#`.
outputFormat: Print the number of tilings (it can be 0).

examples.note: The 2 by 3 board can be covered with two L pieces in 2 ways.

hints: Always cover the first free square in reading order.
Describe each orientation by the offsets of its squares relative to its first square in reading order.
Check the three squares, cover them, recurse, and uncover them.

starter.python:
r, c = map(int, input().split())
board = [input().strip() for _ in range(r)]

explanation: The function finds the first uncovered square, tries the four orientations of the L-piece whose first square (in reading order) is that square, covers its three squares when they are free and inside the board, recurses, and uncovers them.
solution.complexity: Time proportional to the number of partial tilings (small for 6 by 6), space O(r * c).
